title: Private Edge Gateway guided setup flow, install steps, and upgrade rollback screens
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design ticket for producing a compact, developer-friendly guided setup flow for the Private Edge Gateway (PEG) installer, a set of high-fidelity install screens for the Console and CLI complement, and a clear, testable upgrade + rollback UI pattern for Private deployments. This is focused on the networking flow, stepwise install diagnostics, and an unobtrusive rollback experience that Surface operators can rely on during upgrades.
goals: Reduce first-time setup time for PEG by 35% through clearer step boundaries and inline diagnostics
Provide a single sequence of Console screens that map 1:1 to the CLI installer output to reduce operator confusion
Design a safe upgrade modal with staged rollback affordances and clear recovery steps
deliverables: 6 high-fidelity Console screens (intro, network validation, credentials, progress, success, rollback modal)
3 CLI-adjacent screenshot sets showing equivalent prompts and success/failure output
SVG asset pack for network topology illustrations (edge, transit, private CIDR overlays)
Annotated microcopy file with copy variants for toned vs. direct language
screens: Intro: single-panel risk summary + pre-check checklist with expandable details
Network validation: automatic CIDR detection, NAT/route warnings, test endpoint probe results
Credentials step: SSH key paste + KMS binding step with inline link to key rotation docs
Installer progress: streaming log tail + staged phases (Download -> Install -> Configure -> Test)
Success: topology map with interactive CIDR overlay and suggested next steps
Upgrade modal: expected impact, backout window control, dry-run toggle, and rollback button
decisions: Use progressive disclosure for advanced network options (show advanced toggles only after a failed probe)
Show streaming installer logs but hide verbose debug by default; expose a 'Show debug output' toggle
Implement rollback as a first-class modal with a required confirmation step and clear timeline for automated backout
Design illustrations that are abstract (no provider logos) to keep assets reusable across cloud regions
tradeoffs: Hiding verbose logs reduces cognitive load but can delay root-cause for operators; mitigated by adding a single-step 'copy logs' CTA
Adding a dry-run option increases complexity in the UI but significantly reduces upgrade failures for less experienced teams
In-product KMS binding guidance requires sensitive copy approval which will increase delivery time by one cycle
open_questions: Should the upgrade dry-run be enabled by default for Dedicated customers? (PM decision)
Do we surface historical network topology changes on the success screen, or link to Console 'History' to reduce screen density?
Do we require SSO user to have 'deploy' role before exposing the 'Upgrade' affordance? (security/AM)
What level of installer log retention do we display in Console vs. link to raw archive?
updates: 2026-01-12: Kickoff meeting with Eng (runtime + infra), PM, and Security. Agreed scope and SSO requirement research (action: security to clarify roles).

2026-01-28: First high-fidelity screens uploaded to Figma; linked iconography and SVG exports prepared. Accessibility pass 1 done (contrast adjustments).
2026-02-03: Design review with PM and two customer beta reps. Beta feedback: prefer 'dry-run' on by default for non-prod upgrades. PM to assess telemetry impact.
2026-02-08: Updated mocks addressing copy tone and added rollback confirmation step. Ready for engineering handoff (pending security review).
